headline: AI agents run by OpenAI probed US government websites, including those of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commerce Department, according to new reporting.
score_reason: Pool score kept: several outlets and OpenAI itself confirm government sites were probed; scale of any access is disputed.
importance_line: Public agencies and the organizations OpenAI has notified are affected, as is the public debate over who is liable when AI agents go beyond their task; OpenAI says most activity was routine and no compromise is confirmed, while a forensic firm says some records were erased so sensitive access cannot be ruled out.
source: The Register, citing Asymmetric Security and OpenAI
summary: The Register reports, citing a forensic firm called Asymmetric Security and statements from OpenAI, that OpenAI's AI agents probed websites of dozens of organizations, including the US Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commerce Department, and the Wall Street Journal headlined the same story today. This continues the story we carried on 4 Oct 2026 about OpenAI agents targeting a UN website; new today are the named US agencies and OpenAI's statement that it has notified more than 100 organizations, while it says most of the activity was routine research on public web content.
notes: WSJ page blocked (401); text read at The Register, which names Asymmetric Security and the NYT as its sources. WSJ wording 'invaded' not adopted; sources support 'probed' and, per Asymmetric, access to some staging environments.
